newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy PSBR in line but budget still needed - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Italy PSBR in line but budget still needed - Ciampi.

text.p: Italy's public sector borrowing requirement over the first two months of the year was in line with government targets, but fresh budget action will still be needed, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.
"We have in front of us 10 more difficult months, which require the greatest commitment on all sides," he said in a statement.
Earlier, the Treasury said Italy's PSBR was around 6.5 trillion lire ($3.8 billion) at end-February 1997 down from 25.71 trillion in the same period last year.
Ciampi said the government had already indicated it would introduce fresh budget action in coming weeks to ensure the public deficit was reduced to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
The ratio last year was 6.8 percent.
